title: Fourier support and sums of juntas
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set, let $\pi$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$, and let $B$ be an orthonormal basis of real-valued functions on $\Omega$, indexed by a finite nonempty set and containing the constant-one function as its distinguished zero-indexed element. For a nonnegative integer $n$, let $f:(\mathrm{Fin}\ n\to\Omega)\to\mathbb{R}$ and let $k$ be a nonnegative integer. If every product-basis Fourier coefficient of $f$ indexed by a tuple whose entries differ from the distinguished index in more than $k$ coordinates is zero, then $f$ is a sum, over subsets of the $n$ coordinates, of functions each depending only on the coordinates in its indexing subset, with the summand equal to zero whenever that subset has more than $k$ elements.
hypotheses_covered: Basis $B$ is a real algebraic basis, is orthonormal for the $\pi$-weighted inner product, and has a distinguished constant-one basis vector
Fourier coefficients vanish for every multi-index whose support has size greater than $k$
